passages.text: Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that a census should be taken of the whole empire.
passages.sermon:
Caesar Augustus was the ruler of the Roman Empire.
He gave an order.
He commanded that a census must be taken.
This census included the whole empire.
This happened in those days.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐξῆλθεν δόγμα παρὰ Καίσαρος Αὐγούστου ἀπογράφεσθαι πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην

passages.text: This was the first census to take place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
passages.sermon: Quirinius governed Syria.\r\nThe first census happened during his rule.\r\nThis census took place at that time.
passages.original: αὕτη ἀπογραφὴ πρώτη ἐγένετο ἡγεμονεύοντος τῆς Συρίας Κυρηνίου

passages.text: And everyone went to his own town to register.
passages.sermon:
Caesar Augustus ruled the Roman Empire.
He sent out a decree.
The decree ordered a census of the whole empire.
Everyone obeyed the decree.
Each person traveled to his own town.
Each person went there to register.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπορεύοντο πάντες ἀπογράφεσθαι ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πόλιν

passages.text: So Joseph also went up from Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, since he was from the house and line of David.
passages.sermon:
Joseph lived in Nazareth.
Nazareth was a town in Galilee.
Joseph traveled from Nazareth to Judea.
He went to the city of David.
People called this city Bethlehem.
Joseph belonged to the house of David.
He was from the family line of David.
That is why Joseph went to Bethlehem.
passages.original: Ἀνέβη δὲ καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐκ πόλεως Ναζαρὲθ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν εἰς πόλιν Δαυὶδ ἥτις καλεῖται Βηθλεέμ διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυίδ

passages.text: He went there to register with Mary, who was pledged to him in marriage and was expecting a child.
passages.sermon:
Joseph traveled to Bethlehem.
Mary went with Joseph.
Mary was pledged to marry Joseph.
Mary was expecting a child.
Joseph and Mary went to Bethlehem to register.
passages.original: ἀπογράψασθαι σὺν Μαριὰμ τῇ ἐμνηστευμένῃ αὐτῷ οὔσῃ ἐγκύῳ

passages.text: While they were there, the time came for her Child to be born.
passages.sermon: Mary and Joseph were in Bethlehem.\r\nMary was expecting a child.\r\nThe time arrived for Mary to give birth.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν

passages.text: And she gave birth to her firstborn, a Son. She wrapped Him in swaddling cloths and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
passages.sermon:
Mary was pledged to Joseph in marriage.
Mary was expecting a child.
Mary gave birth to her first son.
She wrapped her son in swaddling cloths.
She laid her son in a manger.
There was no room for them in the inn.
passages.original: καὶ ἔτεκεν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς τὸν πρωτότοκον καὶ ἐσπαργάνωσεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀνέκλινεν αὐτὸν ἐν φάτνῃ διότι οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τόπος ἐν τῷ καταλύματι

passages.text: And there were shepherds residing in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks by night.
passages.sermon: Shepherds lived in the same region.\r\nThey stayed out in the fields at night.\r\nThey watched over their flocks during the night.
passages.original: Καὶ ποιμένες ἦσαν ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῇ αὐτῇ ἀγραυλοῦντες καὶ φυλάσσοντες φυλακὰς τῆς νυκτὸς ἐπὶ τὴν ποίμνην αὐτῶν

passages.text: Just then an angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
passages.sermon: An angel from the Lord appeared to the shepherds.\r\nThe glory of the Lord shone all around the shepherds.\r\nThe shepherds became very afraid.
passages.original: καὶ ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἐπέστη αὐτοῖς καὶ δόξα Κυρίου περιέλαμψεν αὐτούς καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν

passages.text: But the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid! For behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people: Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord!
passages.sermon:
An angel of the Lord spoke to the shepherds.
The angel said, "Do not be afraid."
I bring you good news.
This news will bring great joy.
This joy is for all people.
Today, a Savior has been born to you.
He was born in the city of David.
He is Christ the Lord.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ ἄγγελος Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ἰδοὺ γὰρ εὐαγγελίζομαι ὑμῖν χαρὰν μεγάλην ἥτις ἔσται παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ὅτι ἐτέχθη ὑμῖν σήμερον Σωτήρ ὅς ἐστιν Χριστὸς Κύριος ἐν πόλει Δαυίδ

passages.text: And this will be a sign to you: You will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”
passages.sermon:
The angel spoke to the shepherds.
The angel gave them a sign.
They would find a baby.
The baby would be wrapped in swaddling cloths.
The baby would be lying in a manger.
passages.original: καὶ τοῦτο ὑμῖν τὸ σημεῖον εὑρήσετε βρέφος ἐσπαργανωμένον καὶ κείμενον ἐν φάτνῃ

passages.text: And suddenly there appeared with the angel a great multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men on whom His favor rests!”
passages.sermon:
A great multitude of angels appeared suddenly.
These angels came with the first angel.
These angels belonged to the heavenly host.
They praised God.
They said, “Glory to God in the highest.”
They also said, “On earth peace to men on whom His favor rests.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξαίφνης ἐγένετο σὺν τῷ ἀγγέλῳ πλῆθος στρατιᾶς οὐρανίου αἰνούντων τὸν Θεὸν καὶ λεγόντων Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκίας

passages.text: When the angels had left them and gone into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
passages.sermon:
The angels left the shepherds.
The angels went into heaven.
The shepherds spoke to each other.
The shepherds said, “Let us go to Bethlehem.”
The shepherds said, “Let us see this thing that has happened.”
The Lord has made this thing known to us.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἀπῆλθον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οἱ ἄγγελοι οἱ ποιμένες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους Διέλθωμεν δὴ ἕως Βηθλεὲμ καὶ ἴδωμεν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο τὸ γεγονὸς ὃ ὁ Κύριος ἐγνώρισεν ἡμῖν

passages.text: So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph and the Baby, who was lying in the manger.
passages.sermon:
The shepherds acted quickly.
They went to Bethlehem.
They found Mary.
They found Joseph.
They found the Baby.
The Baby was lying in the manger.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦλθαν σπεύσαντες καὶ ἀνεῦραν τήν τε Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ καὶ τὸ βρέφος κείμενον ἐν τῇ φάτνῃ

passages.text: After they had seen the Child, they spread the message they had received about Him.
passages.sermon: The shepherds saw the Child.\r\nThey had received a message about this Child from the angels.\r\nThe shepherds spread this message to others.
passages.original: ἰδόντες δὲ ἐγνώρισαν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ λαληθέντος αὐτοῖς περὶ τοῦ παιδίου τούτου

passages.text: And all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them.
passages.sermon:
The shepherds spoke to the people.
The people listened to the shepherds.
Everyone who heard the message felt amazed.
The message came from the shepherds.
passages.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν περὶ τῶν λαληθέντων ὑπὸ τῶν ποιμένων πρὸς αὐτούς

passages.text: But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart.
passages.sermon:
Mary was the mother of Jesus.
Mary heard everything that happened about her Son.
Mary remembered all these things.
Mary kept these things safe in her heart.
Mary thought deeply about them.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ Μαρία πάντα συνετήρει τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα συμβάλλουσα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς

passages.text: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, which was just as the angel had told them.
passages.sermon:
The shepherds returned.
They glorified God.
They praised God.
They did this because of everything they had heard.
They did this because of everything they had seen.
Everything happened just as the angel had told them.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑπέστρεψαν οἱ ποιμένες δοξάζοντες καὶ αἰνοῦντες τὸν Θεὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἤκουσαν καὶ εἶδον καθὼς ἐλαλήθη πρὸς αὐτούς

passages.text: When the eight days until His circumcision had passed, He was named Jesus, the name the angel had given Him before He had been conceived.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a baby boy.
His parents waited eight days after His birth.
They circumcised Him on the eighth day.
They gave Him the name Jesus.
An angel had given this name before He was conceived.
The angel spoke this name to His parents.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ τοῦ περιτεμεῖν αὐτόν καὶ ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦς τὸ κληθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγγέλου πρὸ τοῦ συλλημφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ

passages.text: And when the time of purification according to the Law of Moses was complete, His parents brought Him to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord (as it is written in the Law of the Lord: “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”), and to offer the sacrifice specified in the Law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a firstborn male child.
His parents were Mary and Joseph.
The Law of Moses required purification after childbirth.
The time for their purification ended.
Mary and Joseph obeyed the Law of Moses.
They brought Jesus to Jerusalem.
They presented Jesus to the Lord in the temple.
The Law of the Lord says every firstborn male must be consecrated to the Lord.
The Law also commands a sacrifice.
The sacrifice is a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
Mary and Joseph offered this sacrifice for Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παραστῆσαι τῷ Κυρίῳ καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν νόμῳ Κυρίου ὅτι Πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ Κυρίῳ κληθήσεται καὶ τοῦ δοῦναι θυσίαν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Κυρίου Ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νοσσοὺς περιστερῶν

passages.text: Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
passages.sermon:
A man lived in Jerusalem.
His name was Simeon.
Simeon was righteous.
Simeon was devout.
He waited for the consolation of Israel.
The Holy Spirit was upon Simeon.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος ἦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τοῦ Ἰσραήλ καὶ Πνεῦμα ἦν Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
passages.sermon:
Simeon was a man in Jerusalem.
Simeon was righteous and devout.
The Holy Spirit was upon Simeon.
The Holy Spirit revealed something to Simeon.
The Holy Spirit told Simeon he would not die before he saw the Lord’s Christ.
passages.original: καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχρηματισμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον πρὶν ἢ ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν Κυρίου

passages.text: Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple courts. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for Him what was customary under the Law, Simeon took Him in his arms and blessed God, saying: “Sovereign Lord, as You have promised, You now dismiss Your servant in peace.
passages.sermon:
Simeon was a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem.
The Holy Spirit was upon Simeon.
The Holy Spirit led Simeon into the temple courts.
The parents of Jesus brought the child Jesus into the temple.
They came to do for Jesus what was customary under the Law.
Simeon took Jesus in his arms.
Simeon blessed God.
Simeon said, “Sovereign Lord, You have promised this.”
“Now You dismiss Your servant in peace.”
passages.original: καὶ ἦλθεν ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι εἰς τὸ ἱερόν καὶ ἐν τῷ εἰσαγαγεῖν τοὺς γονεῖς τὸ παιδίον Ἰησοῦν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτοὺς κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον τοῦ νόμου περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδέξατο αὐτὸ εἰς τὰς ἀγκάλας καὶ εὐλόγησεν τὸν Θεὸν καὶ εἶπεν Νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν σου Δέσποτα κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ

passages.text: For my eyes have seen Your salvation, which You have prepared in the sight of all people, a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Your people Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Simeon was a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem.
The Holy Spirit had revealed to Simeon that he would not die before seeing the Lord’s Christ.
Simeon saw the child Jesus in the temple.
Simeon spoke to God.
Simeon said, “My eyes have seen Your salvation.”
God prepared this salvation for all people to see.
This salvation is a light to reveal truth to the Gentiles.
This salvation brings glory to Your people Israel.
passages.original: ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν λαῶν φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: The Child’s father and mother were amazed at what was spoken about Him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the father of Jesus.
Mary was the mother of Jesus.
People spoke words about Jesus.
Joseph and Mary heard these words.
Joseph and Mary were amazed.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλουμένοις περὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then Simeon blessed them and said to His mother Mary: “Behold, this Child is appointed to cause the rise and fall of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be spoken against, so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed— and a sword will pierce your soul as well.”
passages.sermon:
Simeon was a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem.
Simeon blessed Joseph and Mary.
Simeon spoke to Mary, the mother of Jesus.
Simeon said, “This Child is appointed for the fall of many in Israel.
This Child is also appointed for the rise of many in Israel.
This Child will be a sign that people will oppose.
A sword will pierce your own soul, Mary.
God will reveal the thoughts of many hearts through this Child.”
passages.original: καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς Συμεὼν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Μαριὰμ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ Ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ εἰς σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον καὶ σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί

passages.text: There was also a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, who was well along in years. She had been married for seven years, and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, but worshiped night and day, fasting and praying.
passages.sermon:
Anna was a prophetess.
She was the daughter of Phanuel.
She belonged to the tribe of Asher.
Anna was very old.
She had lived with her husband for seven years after her marriage.
Her husband died.
Anna was a widow until she was eighty-four years old.
She never left the temple.
Anna worshiped God night and day.
She fasted and prayed continually.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν Ἅννα προφῆτις θυγάτηρ Φανουήλ ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσήρ αὕτη προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἔτη ἑπτὰ ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν

passages.text: Coming forward at that moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Anna was a prophetess.
She was the daughter of Phanuel.
She belonged to the tribe of Asher.
Anna was very old.
She came forward at that moment.
She gave thanks to God.
She spoke about the Child.
She spoke to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐπιστᾶσα ἀνθωμολογεῖτο τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς προσδεχομένοις λύτρωσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: When Jesus’ parents had done everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had parents named Mary and Joseph.
They obeyed the Law of the Lord.
They did everything the Law required.
After this, they returned to Galilee.
They went to their own town.
Their town was called Nazareth.
passages.original: Καὶ ὡς ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸν νόμον Κυρίου ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς πόλιν ἑαυτῶν Ναζαρέθ

passages.text: And the Child grew and became strong. He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a child.
He grew.
He became strong.
He was full of wisdom.
God’s grace was on Him.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πληρούμενον σοφίᾳ καὶ χάρις Θεοῦ ἦν ἐπ’ αὐτό

passages.text: Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had parents.
\r\nHis parents went to Jerusalem every year.
\r\nThey went for the Feast of the Passover.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπορεύοντο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἔτος εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῇ ἑορτῇ τοῦ πάσχα

passages.text: And when He was twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the Feast.
passages.sermon: Jesus was twelve years old.\r\nHis parents followed the custom of the Feast of the Passover.\r\nThey went up to Jerusalem for the Feast.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἐτῶν δώδεκα ἀναβαινόντων αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἑορτῆς

passages.text: When those days were over and they were returning home, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a boy.
His parents finished the days of the Feast in Jerusalem.
They began to return home.
Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem.
His parents did not know that Jesus had stayed.
passages.original: καὶ τελειωσάντων τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ὑποστρέφειν αὐτοὺς ὑπέμεινεν Ἰησοῦς ὁ παῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Assuming He was in their company, they traveled on for a day before they began to look for Him among their relatives and friends.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a twelve-year-old boy.
\r\nHis parents thought Jesus was with their group.
\r\nThey traveled for one day.
\r\nAfter one day, they began to look for Jesus.
\r\nThey searched for Him among their relatives.
\r\nThey also searched for Him among their friends.
passages.original: νομίσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ συνοδίᾳ ἦλθον ἡμέρας ὁδὸν καὶ ἀνεζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γνωστοῖς

passages.text: When they could not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem to search for Him.
passages.sermon:
Mary and Joseph were the parents of Jesus.
They could not find Jesus among their relatives and friends.
They returned to Jerusalem.
They searched for Jesus in Jerusalem.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀναζητοῦντες αὐτόν

passages.text: Finally, after three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a twelve-year-old boy.
His parents searched for Him.
After three days, they found Him.
They found Him in the temple.
He was sitting among the teachers.
He listened to the teachers.
He asked the teachers questions.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς εὗρον αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καθεζόμενον ἐν μέσῳ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀκούοντα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶντα αὐτούς

passages.text: And all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a twelve-year-old boy.
He sat among the teachers in the temple.
He listened to the teachers.
He asked the teachers questions.
Many people heard Jesus speak.
Everyone who heard Him felt amazed.
They saw His great understanding.
They heard His wise answers.
passages.original: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ συνέσει καὶ ταῖς ἀποκρίσεσιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When His parents saw Him, they were astonished. “Child, why have You done this to us?” His mother asked. “Your father and I have been anxiously searching for You.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a twelve-year-old boy.
His parents were Mary and Joseph.
His parents had been searching for Him for three days.
They found Jesus in the temple.
When His parents saw Him, they were astonished.
His mother spoke to Him.
She said, “Child, why have You done this to us?”
She said, “Your father and I have been anxiously searching for You.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεπλάγησαν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ Τέκνον τί ἐποίησας ἡμῖν οὕτως ἰδοὺ ὁ πατήρ σου κἀγὼ ὀδυνώμενοι ἐζητοῦμέν σε

passages.text: “Why were you looking for Me?” He asked. “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house ?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a boy.
Jesus spoke to His parents.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, “Why were you looking for Me?”
He gave them another question.
He said, “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house?”
Jesus called God His Father.
Jesus said He must be in God’s house.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με οὐκ ᾔδειτε ὅτι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Πατρός μου δεῖ εἶναί με

passages.text: But they did not understand the statement He was making to them.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His parents.\r\nHis parents did not understand His words.\r\nThey did not know what He meant.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐ συνῆκαν τὸ ῥῆμα ὃ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. But His mother treasured up all these things in her heart.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a boy.
Jesus went down to Nazareth with His parents.
Jesus obeyed His parents.
His mother was Mary.
Mary remembered all these things.
Mary kept these things in her heart.
passages.original: Καὶ κατέβη μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρὲθ καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ διετήρει πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς

passages.text: And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a boy in Nazareth.
Jesus grew wiser.
Jesus became taller and older.
God favored Jesus.
People also favored Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ Ἰησοῦς προέκοπτεν ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ Θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις
